reading.body:
Alpine Group Partners filed 42 AI lobbying reports, and its largest AI client by filing count is the Recording Industry Association of America, not a technology or energy company.

The client list is the useful part. A music industry trade group leads at 15 AI filings, ahead of a defense contractor at 8 and Siemens at 6. A business roundtable, a philanthropic network, a toy association, and a health security certifier follow. Two electric utilities, Duke Energy and Vistra, appear once each. That spread says AI lobbying is not confined to AI companies. Trade groups and incumbents in media, defense, manufacturing, and toys are all paying a Washington firm to track the issue.

The utility filings are the thinnest signal here and should be read that way. One filing each for Duke Energy and Vistra is enough to show they are watching AI policy, but not enough to say what they want from it. Anyone looking for evidence that power companies are lobbying on data center demand will not find it in these counts.

The data also cannot say what any client argued. A filing records that a firm lobbied on an issue, not the position taken, so the counts measure attention rather than intent. The lobbyist totals, led by Curtis Philip at 28 filings and Jennifer Forrest at 25, show who is doing the work, not which client each filing served.

summary: ALPINE GROUP PARTNERS, LLC. filed 42 Lobbying Disclosure Act reports on AI held by this site. Its clients, the lobbyists named on those filings and the AI bills they name are below. LDA registrant id 1171.
